title: Body regions
summary: Explore 52 anterior and posterior worksheet targets. Connect anatomical terms to familiar body regions, then practice identifying and locating them.

targets.name: Frons
targets.teach: The forehead is the front of the head above the eyes.
targets.memory: Picture the FRONT of a cap resting on your forehead.
targets.spelling: FRONT-al keeps FRONT in view. Frons ends in -ons.

targets.name: Cranium
targets.teach: The skull encloses and protects the brain.
targets.memory: A cranium is a protective crash helmet for the brain.
targets.spelling: Break cranium into CRA-NI-UM; cranial keeps CRANI-.

targets.name: Facies
targets.teach: The face includes the eyes, nose, and mouth used in sensing and expression.
targets.memory: FACE → FACial: keep the FAC together.
targets.spelling: Facies ends in -ies; facial is FACE with the ending changed.

targets.name: Oris
targets.teach: The mouth takes in food and helps form speech.
targets.memory: ORal reports come out of your mouth.
targets.spelling: Oris ends in -is, not -us. Oral keeps OR-.

targets.name: Mentis
targets.teach: Here mental names the chin region, not a thought process.
targets.memory: Rest your chin on your hand while doing MENTal math.
targets.spelling: Mentis ends in -is; mental keeps MENT-.

targets.name: Axilla
targets.teach: The axilla is the area beneath the shoulder where arm and trunk meet.
targets.memory: Picture two L-shaped arms lifted to expose the armpits.
targets.spelling: Axilla has one x and two l letters: AX-ILL-A.

targets.name: Brachium
targets.teach: In regional anatomy, the arm is the shoulder-to-elbow segment.
targets.memory: Brace a bag against your BRACHium, your upper arm.
targets.spelling: Brachium: BRACH-I-UM. Brachial keeps BRACHI-.

targets.name: Antecubitis
targets.teach: This is the front of the elbow, not the bony point at the back.
targets.memory: ANTE = front: picture the front elbow crease facing you.
targets.spelling: Antecubitis: ANTE-CUB-ITIS. Antecubital: ANTE-CUB-ITAL.

targets.name: Antebrachium
targets.teach: The forearm is the elbow-to-wrist segment.
targets.memory: Build the longer word by putting ANTE before BRACHIUM.
targets.spelling: Antebrachium = ANTE + BRACHIUM. Do not lose the h.

targets.name: Carpus
targets.teach: The wrist connects hand and forearm and allows the hand to bend.
targets.memory: Picture your wrist turning a CAR steering wheel: CAR → CARpus.
targets.spelling: CAR-pus uses a, not o. Carpal shares the same CARP stem.

targets.name: Pollex
targets.teach: The thumb opposes the fingers to help grip objects.
targets.memory: Give a thumbs-up to a POLL: POLL + EX.
targets.spelling: Pollex has two l letters and ends in -ex.

targets.name: Palma
targets.teach: The palm is the inner surface of the hand used in gripping.
targets.memory: The familiar word PALM is already inside both answers.
targets.spelling: Palma = PALM + A; palmar = PALM + AR.

targets.name: Digits
targets.teach: Fingers help grip and manipulate objects; their bones are phalanges.
targets.memory: PHingers is a deliberately silly spelling cue for PHalanges.
targets.spelling: Phalanges starts PH, not f: PHAL-ANG-ES. Phalangeal keeps PHALANGE-.

targets.name: Patella
targets.teach: The patella protects the front of the knee and helps the thigh muscles extend it.
targets.memory: TELL a story about bumping your kneecap: pa-TELL-a.
targets.spelling: Patella has one t and two l letters: PA-TELL-A.

targets.name: Crus
targets.teach: The leg region runs from knee to ankle, rather than the whole lower limb.
targets.memory: Picture CRUsing from knee to ankle.
targets.spelling: Crus ends in -us; crural is CRUR-AL.

targets.name: Tarsus
targets.teach: The ankle region joins the leg and foot and contributes to walking.
targets.memory: Imagine stepping into TAR around your ankle.
targets.spelling: Tarsus: TAR-SUS. Tarsal shares TARS-.

targets.name: Digits
targets.teach: Toes help balance and push-off; their bones are phalanges.
targets.memory: Count your toe DIGITS like digits on a counter.
targets.spelling: Phalanges starts PH and ends -anges. Digital keeps DIGIT-.

targets.name: Hallux
targets.teach: The great toe contributes to balance and push-off in walking.
targets.memory: Your big toe leads you down the HALL: HALL + UX.
targets.spelling: Hallux has two l letters and ends in x: HALL-UX.

targets.name: Oculus
targets.teach: The eye detects light for vision.
targets.memory: Imagine a tiny O-shaped lens at the start of Oculus.
targets.spelling: Oculus is OC-U-LUS; ocular keeps OCUL-. Orbital names the eye region.

targets.name: Bucca
targets.teach: The cheeks form the sides of the mouth and help keep food between the teeth.
targets.memory: Two C-shaped cheeks: buCCa.
targets.spelling: Bucca has two c letters: BUC-CA. Buccal adds l.

targets.name: Auris
targets.teach: The ear is associated with hearing; the inner ear also supports balance.
targets.memory: An AUdio reminder for AUris: both begin AU.
targets.spelling: Auris ends in -is. Otic is O-T-I-C.

targets.name: Nasus
targets.teach: The nose is involved in smell and conditions inhaled air.
targets.memory: NASal spray goes in the nose.
targets.spelling: Nasus ends in -us. Nasal keeps NAS-.

targets.name: Cervicis
targets.teach: Here the cervical region is the neck connecting head and trunk.
targets.memory: Keep CERVIC, then choose IS for cervicis or AL for cervical.
targets.spelling: Cervicis: CER-VIC-IS, ending in -is. Cervical: CER-VIC-AL.

targets.name: Thorax
targets.teach: The chest contains the heart and lungs and moves during breathing.
targets.memory: Imagine THOR wearing chest armor: THORax.
targets.spelling: Thorax ends in x; thoracic is THOR-AC-IC. Keep the h after t.

targets.name: Mamma
targets.teach: Mammary glands in the breast can produce milk.
targets.memory: MAM-MA: two short chunks, with the m repeated at the join.
targets.spelling: Mamma has three m letters altogether: MAM-MA. Mammary keeps MAMM-.

targets.name: Abdomen
targets.teach: The abdomen contains many digestive organs.
targets.memory: Think ABDO before your abdominal exercise.
targets.spelling: Abdomen: AB-DO-MEN. Abdominal changes the ending to -inal.

targets.name: Umbilicus
targets.teach: The navel marks the former attachment of the umbilical cord.
targets.memory: Connect UMBILicus to the UMBILical cord.
targets.spelling: Umbilicus: UM-BIL-I-CUS. Umbilical keeps UMBILIC-.

targets.name: Hip
targets.teach: The hip region is where the thigh meets the pelvis.
targets.memory: Picture an X beside the hip: coXal.
targets.spelling: Coxal has an x: COX-AL. Coxa ends in a.

targets.name: Pelvis
targets.teach: The pelvis supports and transfers body weight toward the lower limbs.
targets.memory: PELVI stays put while S changes to C.
targets.spelling: Pelvis ends in -is; pelvic ends in -ic.

targets.name: Inguen
targets.teach: The groin is the junction of the upper thigh and trunk.
targets.memory: Keep INGU together in both inguen and inguinal.
targets.spelling: Ing uen written together is INGUEN. Inguinal: IN-GUIN-AL.

targets.name: Pubis
targets.teach: The pubic region lies at the front of the pelvis.
targets.memory: PUBI stays put: pubi-S or pubi-C.
targets.spelling: Pubis ends in -is; pubic ends in -ic.

targets.name: Femur
targets.teach: The thigh is the hip-to-knee segment and contains the femur.
targets.memory: The FEMur belongs in the FEMoral thigh region.
targets.spelling: Femur: FE-MUR. Femoral: FEM-OR-AL.

targets.name: Pes
targets.teach: The foot supports weight and helps balance and propulsion.
targets.memory: Your foot presses a PEDal.
targets.spelling: Pes is P-E-S; pedal keeps PED-.

targets.name: Trunk
targets.teach: The trunk includes the chest, abdomen, and pelvis.
targets.memory: A tree trunk is its central support; your torso is your central body region.
targets.spelling: Trunk is the everyday term; torso is TOR-SO.

targets.name: Acromial
targets.teach: The acromial region is at the point of the shoulder.
targets.memory: A CROW perched on your shoulder cues A-CRO-mial.
targets.spelling: Acromial: A-CRO-MI-AL. Acromion ends in -ion.

targets.name: Dorsum
targets.teach: The dorsal region is the back of the trunk.
targets.memory: A dorsal fin is on a fish’s back: DORS → back.
targets.spelling: Dorsum ends in -um; dorsal keeps DORS-.

targets.name: Brachium
targets.teach: In regional anatomy, the arm is the shoulder-to-elbow segment.
targets.memory: Brace a bag against your BRACHium, your upper arm.
targets.spelling: Brachium: BRACH-I-UM. Brachial keeps BRACHI-.

targets.name: Olecranon
targets.teach: The olecranon forms the bony point at the back of the elbow.
targets.memory: “Oh!” when you bump your elbow cues O-lecranon.
targets.spelling: Olecranon: O-LE-CRA-NON. Olecranal ends in -al.

targets.name: Lumbus
targets.teach: The lumbar region is the lower back between the ribs and pelvis.
targets.memory: A LUMbar cushion supports the lower back.
targets.spelling: Lumbus: LUM-BUS. Lumbar changes -us to -ar.

targets.name: Sacrum
targets.teach: The sacral region overlies the sacrum at the back of the pelvis.
targets.memory: Picture a SAC-shaped cushion at the back of the pelvis.
targets.spelling: Sacrum: SAC-RUM. Sacral keeps SACR-.

targets.name: Antebrachium
targets.teach: The forearm is the elbow-to-wrist segment.
targets.memory: Build the longer word by putting ANTE before BRACHIUM.
targets.spelling: Antebrachium = ANTE + BRACHIUM. Do not lose the h.

targets.name: Manus
targets.teach: The hand grips, manipulates, and senses objects.
targets.memory: MANUal work is done by hand.
targets.spelling: Manus ends in -us; manual keeps MANU-.

targets.name: Gluteus
targets.teach: The gluteal region covers muscles that move and stabilize the hip.
targets.memory: Think of your GLUTE muscles when standing from a chair.
targets.spelling: Gluteus: GLU-TE-US. Gluteal keeps GLUTE-.

targets.name: Femur
targets.teach: The thigh is the hip-to-knee segment and contains the femur.
targets.memory: The FEMur belongs in the FEMoral thigh region.
targets.spelling: Femur: FE-MUR. Femoral: FEM-OR-AL.

targets.name: Popliteus
targets.teach: This label identifies the back of the knee, not the kneecap.
targets.memory: Picture a POP of light behind your knee: POP-LIT.
targets.spelling: Popliteus: POP-LIT-E-US. Popliteal: POP-LIT-E-AL.

targets.name: Sura
targets.teach: Calf muscles help lift the heel and push off during walking.
targets.memory: Picture the calf SUrging upward when you rise onto your toes.
targets.spelling: Sura: SU-RA. Sural adds l.

targets.name: Calcaneus
targets.teach: The calcaneus forms the heel and helps bear weight.
targets.memory: A CAN under your heel cues cal-CAN-eus.
targets.spelling: Calcaneus: CAL-CAN-E-US. Calcaneal keeps CALCANE-.

targets.name: Planta
targets.teach: The sole contacts the ground and supports the foot during standing and walking.
targets.memory: PLANT your foot on the ground: PLANTar.
targets.spelling: Planta = PLANT + A; plantar = PLANT + AR.

targets.name: Cephalon
targets.teach: The head contains the brain and several major sensory organs.
targets.memory: Picture a cap marked CEPH on your head.
targets.spelling: Cephalon: CEPH-AL-ON. Cephalic: CEPH-AL-IC.

targets.name: Cervicis
targets.teach: Here the cervical region is the neck connecting head and trunk.
targets.memory: Keep CERVIC, then choose IS for cervicis or AL for cervical.
targets.spelling: Cervicis: CER-VIC-IS, ending in -is. Cervical: CER-VIC-AL.

targets.name: Upper limb
targets.teach: This includes the arm, forearm, and hand.
targets.memory: The upper limb reaches from shoulder to fingertips.
targets.spelling: Upper extremity: EX-TREM-I-TY. Limb has a silent b.

targets.name: Lower limb
targets.teach: This includes the thigh, leg, and foot.
targets.memory: The lower limb reaches from hip to toes.
targets.spelling: Lower extremity: EX-TREM-I-TY. Limb has a silent b.

title: Body cavities
summary: Trace the dorsal and ventral compartments, then connect each subdivision to the structures it protects.

targets.name: Cranial cavity
targets.teach: Inside the skull; houses the brain. Part of the dorsal body cavity.

targets.name: Vertebral cavity
targets.teach: Within the vertebral canal; houses the spinal cord. Also called the spinal cavity.

targets.name: Thoracic cavity
targets.teach: Superior to the diaphragm. Contains the two pleural compartments and the mediastinum.

targets.name: Superior mediastinum
targets.teach: The superior portion of the central thoracic compartment between the lungs. The heart lies in the middle mediastinum, inferior to this region.

targets.name: Pleural cavity
targets.teach: A thin potential space between visceral and parietal pleura surrounding each lung; normally contains a film of serous fluid.

targets.name: Pericardial cavity
targets.teach: The thin fluid-containing space between the layers of serous pericardium; located within the mediastinum.

targets.name: Diaphragm
targets.teach: A dome-shaped skeletal muscle separating the thoracic and abdominopelvic cavities; contracts during inspiration.

targets.name: Abdominal cavity
targets.teach: The superior part of the abdominopelvic cavity. Contains many digestive organs; kidneys lie behind the parietal peritoneum.

targets.name: Pelvic cavity
targets.teach: The inferior part of the abdominopelvic cavity; contains the urinary bladder, rectum and internal reproductive structures.

targets.name: Dorsal body cavity
targets.teach: The posterior compartment comprising the cranial and vertebral cavities; protects the brain and spinal cord.

targets.name: Ventral body cavity
targets.teach: The anterior compartment comprising the thoracic and abdominopelvic cavities. The diaphragm separates its two main divisions.

targets.name: Abdominopelvic cavity
targets.teach: The continuous space formed by the abdominal and pelvic cavities, inferior to the diaphragm.

title: Membranes
summary: Learn the serous layers first, then distinguish the major membrane types. Detailed tissue membranes and meninges extend beyond Chapters 1–2 and are marked as extension material.

views.title: Serous membranes · heart & balloon

targets.name: Visceral pericardium
targets.teach: The serous layer directly on the heart surface; also called the epicardium. Think: visceral hugs the viscera.

targets.name: Pericardial cavity
targets.teach: The narrow space between serous layers. It contains lubricating fluid, not air.

targets.name: Parietal pericardium
targets.teach: The outer serous layer lining the inner surface of the fibrous pericardium. Think: parietal lines the perimeter.

views.title: Pleural membranes · lung detail

targets.name: Parietal pleura
targets.teach: Lines the inner thoracic wall, mediastinum and superior surface of the diaphragm.

targets.name: Visceral pleura
targets.teach: Closely covers the lung surface, including its fissures.

targets.name: Pleural cavity
targets.teach: The thin space between visceral and parietal pleura; normally contains a film of serous fluid.

views.note: A later-chapter illustration makes the Chapter 1 pleural layers easier to distinguish. The enlarged inset separates the layers for visibility; the real space is very thin.

views.title: Peritoneal membranes · transverse section

targets.name: Visceral peritoneum
targets.teach: Covers the external surfaces of intraperitoneal organs. It reflects into folds that support viscera.

targets.name: Parietal peritoneum
targets.teach: Lines the inner abdominopelvic wall.

targets.name: Peritoneal cavity
targets.teach: A potential space between serous surfaces containing lubricating fluid. It is not the entire abdominal cavity.

views.note: Notice the kidneys behind the peritoneal lining: retroperitoneal means posterior to the peritoneum. This later-chapter figure illustrates the Chapter 1 layers.

views.title: Extension · meninges

targets.name: Dura mater
targets.teach: The tough outer meninx adjacent to the skull. Cranial dura has periosteal and meningeal layers.

targets.name: Arachnoid mater
targets.teach: The middle meninx, superficial to the cerebrospinal-fluid-filled subarachnoid space.

targets.name: Pia mater
targets.teach: The delicate innermost meninx; follows the brain surface into grooves.

title: Abdominal regions & quadrants
summary: Practice the nine abdominal regions and four quadrants. Region boundaries are reference lines; organs can span several regions.

targets.name: Right hypochondriac region
targets.teach: Under the right costal margin; includes part of the liver and gallbladder.

targets.name: Epigastric region
targets.teach: Upper middle region; includes portions of the stomach and liver.

targets.name: Left hypochondriac region
targets.teach: Under the left costal margin; includes the spleen and part of the stomach.

targets.name: Right lumbar region
targets.teach: Middle right region; includes the ascending colon.

targets.name: Umbilical region
targets.teach: Central region around the navel; includes loops of small intestine.

targets.name: Left lumbar region
targets.teach: Middle left region; includes the descending colon.

targets.name: Right iliac region
targets.teach: Lower right region, also called right inguinal; typically includes the cecum and appendix.

targets.name: Hypogastric region
targets.teach: Lower middle region, also called pubic; contains the urinary bladder, especially when distended.

targets.name: Left iliac region
targets.teach: Lower left region, also called left inguinal; includes the sigmoid colon.

targets.name: Right upper quadrant
targets.teach: RUQ: much of the liver and the gallbladder.

targets.name: Left upper quadrant
targets.teach: LUQ: stomach, spleen and part of the pancreas.

targets.name: Right lower quadrant
targets.teach: RLQ: cecum and appendix; right ovary and uterine tube in female anatomy.

targets.name: Left lower quadrant
targets.teach: LLQ: sigmoid colon; left ovary and uterine tube in female anatomy.

title: Body planes
summary: Identify a plane by the portions it separates, not by the direction you happen to view it from.

views.title: Four ways to section the body

targets.name: Sagittal plane
targets.teach: Divides a body or organ into right and left portions. Midsagittal means equal right and left halves. In 3D, rotate toward the side to see this vertical surface running from front to back.

targets.name: Frontal plane
targets.teach: Divides anterior and posterior portions. Also called the coronal plane. Trace the highlighted plane from shoulder to shoulder, separating the chest from the back.

targets.name: Transverse plane
targets.teach: Divides superior and inferior portions. Produces a cross section.

targets.name: Oblique plane
targets.teach: Passes through the body at an angle to the standard planes.

views.note: Follow the highlighted surface, not the crossing label lines. Sagittal runs front to back through the midline; frontal runs side to side.

title: Directions & position
summary: Use anatomical position as the fixed reference: upright, facing forward, arms at the sides, palms forward, and feet directed forward.
